summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Sanjay Shakya earned a master's degree from Tribhuvan University in 2008–2009. In 2024, he was appointed Assistant Professor at Lumbini Buddhist University.

Historian Sanjay Subrahmanyam studied at St. Stephen's College, the Delhi School of Economics, and the University of Delhi. He held positions at Oxford, the EHESS, UCLA, and the Collège de France, where he was Chair in Early Modern Global History.
Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan studied under teacher M. K. Ganguli (attested 1994) and traditional teacher A. P. Lama.

Indologist and religious studies scholar Sanjukta Gupta studied at Calcutta, Visva-Bharati, and Utrecht under Jan Gonda. She held academic posts at Visva-Bharati, Calcutta, Jadavpur (~1962–1967), Utrecht (~1971–1986), and Oxford (~1987).

Specializing in Indology and history/archaeology, Sanjukta Poddar completed an MA and PhD at the University of Chicago (2015–2022). She served as a postdoctoral teaching fellow at Chicago (2022) before becoming Assistant Professor at Leiden University in 2023.

Working in Indology and religious studies, Sanne Dokter-Mersch completed her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021) under Peter C. Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi, continuing there as a postdoctoral researcher in 2022.

Working in Indology, Santanu Sarkar studied at North Bengal, Cooch Behar Panchanan Barma, Burdwan, and IIT Kharagpur, where he was a PhD scholar (2020–2026). In 2026, he became Assistant Professor at the University of Engineering & Management.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sao Htun Hmat Win studied at Harvard and under Bhaddanta Narada. He taught at Rangoon, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised the Ministry of Religious Affairs (attested 2002).
Sara Frumento is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who pursued a DPhil in Area Studies (South Asia) at Wolfson College, Oxford, and held a post at the University of Oxford (attested 2026).

Working in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, Sara Grant studied at Oxford and Mumbai under Richard De Smet. She taught at Sophia College (~1956–1972) and Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth, and was co-acharya at Christa Prema Seva Ashram (~1972–2000).

Sara L. McClintock, a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, studied at Columbia, CIHTS, Lausanne, and Harvard (PhD, 2002). She held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2003) and Emory University (attested 2026).

Working in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, Sarah Aoife Richardson earned her PhD from the University of Toronto (completed 2016) under doctoral supervisor Jenny Purtle and several other teachers.

Sarah Cymbal specializes in history/archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University of Culture and Arts and the Russian-Armenian University, where she held a post while directing the Silk Road art research center.

Specializing in history/archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, Sarah E. Fraser studied at Michigan and Kobe. She held posts as Associate Professor at Northwestern University (1996) and Directrice d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2000).

Sarah H. Jacoby, a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, studied at Yale and the University of Virginia (PhD 2007). She worked at Columbia University (2006–2009) and became an Associate Professor at Northwestern University in 2009.

Sarah Harding is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche and Lama Tenpa. She served on the faculty at Naropa University (~1992–2018) and became a fellow of the Tsadra Foundation (~2001).

Sarah J. Horton specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and served as Assistant Professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).
Sarah Merkle-Schneider is an Indologist who completed an M.A. at the University of Tübingen and held an M.A. post there (attested 2026).

Sarah Shaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. She held affiliations with Oxford's Faculty of Oriental Studies, Wolfson College, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).
Sarah Wells Brooks was an Indology scholar who studied at Radcliffe College in 1892 under the instruction of Charles Rockwell Lanman.
